title: The 10 Best Corded Leaf Blowers
subtitle: Plug-in leaf blowers and 3-in-1 blower vacuums for yards, decks and driveways, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A corded leaf blower runs as long as the outlet does, weighs less than a battery model with the same airflow, and costs less. We ranked 10 best-sellers from WORX, BLACK+DECKER, Sun Joe and CRAFTSMAN on rating, review volume and features (400 CFM or more, a speed control, and a vacuum/mulcher mode). Compare CFM first: it says how much air moves, while MPH only says how fast. None of them comes with the outdoor extension cord you'll need.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Leaf Blower, 3000W High Power Turbine Handheld Electric Leaf Blower with 82 ft Cord
avoid.flag: Claims 3000W from a 110V plug, which a home outlet can't supply
avoid.verdict: A no-name corded blower that claims 3,000 watts. A standard 15-amp, 120-volt household outlet tops out around 1,800 watts, so the headline number can't be true, and the listing also describes a lithium-ion battery on a corded tool.
reasons: 3,000 watts is more than a standard 15-amp household circuit can deliver (about 1,800 W), so the power claim is false on its face.
The cord bullet talks about 'Lithium Ion battery standards' on a plug-in blower, a sign the copy wasn't written for this product.
The 82 ft cord is fixed to the tool and adds 3.4 lb, for a 10 lb total that's heavier than the 600 CFM WORX WG520.
At $99.99 it costs more than every pick on this page, including the WORX WG520 ($75.27) with 600 CFM and 12,600+ reviews.

buyers_guide.q: CFM or MPH: which number matters?
buyers_guide.a: CFM (cubic feet per minute) is how much air the blower moves, so it decides how big a pile you can push. MPH is how fast that air leaves the nozzle, which helps lift wet or stuck leaves. For lawns, compare CFM first. For hard surfaces and matted leaves, a higher MPH helps.

buyers_guide.q: Should I get a 3-in-1 blower vacuum?
buyers_guide.a: If you bag leaves, yes. A 3-in-1 blows leaves into a pile, then vacuums and shreds them so 10 to 18 bags of leaves fit in one. The trade-off is weight (8 to 12.5 lb here against 4 to 7 lb for blower-only models) and less airflow in blower mode on most of them.

buyers_guide.q: What extension cord do I need?
buyers_guide.a: None of these include one. Use an outdoor-rated cord, and go heavier the longer it gets: 16 gauge is fine up to about 50 ft for a 12-amp blower, and 14 or 12 gauge is the safer choice for 100 ft. Most of these blowers have a cord retainer to stop the plug pulling loose.

Corded blowers cost less, weigh less for the same airflow and never stop for a battery. Cordless wins if your yard is far from an outlet or you'd rather not drag a cord around trees and beds. See our cordless leaf blowers page for battery models.

buyers_guide.q: Is a backpack bag worth it?
buyers_guide.a: Only on 3-in-1 models you use to vacuum a lot. A backpack bag moves the weight of collected leaves off the tool and onto your back, which is easier on your arm, but the whole setup is heavier: 11 to 12.5 lb on the two backpack picks here.
